title: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)

sections.label: Guillotine time and budget cut
sections.summary: The guillotine time for Head X, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, is revised to 2.30 pm and a $100 reduction is moved.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: In view of the statements and several clarifications made in Parliament earlier and the amount of time used, I would now revise the guillotine time for Head X – Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth to 2.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100." First, let me just wish all our lady colleagues within the Chamber a Happy Women's Day.

sections.label: MCCY progress since 2012
sections.summary: Since MCCY's inception in 2012, Singapore has made excellent progress in the sports, youth and community sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth's (MCCY's) inception in 2012, Singapore has made excellent progress in the sports, youth and community sectors.

sections.label: MENDAKI preschool education access
sections.summary: An update is sought on MENDAKI's programmes to increase access to quality preschool education and involve the larger community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can we have an update on the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community's (MENDAKI’s) programmes to increase access to quality preschool education and how it can involve the larger community, for instance, parents and preschool professionals, to ensure that children are schooled earlier?

sections.label: MENDAKI tuition and financial help
sections.summary: MENDAKI runs a tuition programme, administers the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy and provides student loans to help students financially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Today, MENDAKI runs a tuition programme, administers the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) and provides student loans to help our students financially.

sections.label: Madrasah support and updates
sections.summary: An update is sought on efforts to strengthen madrasahs, following $1.5 million set aside annually since 2017 and a new Madrasah Al-Arabiah location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2017, the Government announced greater support for the madrasah sector with $1.5 million set aside annually to help madrasah teachers and students in secular subjects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on any other efforts to further strengthen our madrasahs and better equip our madrasahs to produce graduates who are future-ready?

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister had also announced the new location of Madrasah Al-Arabiah in Toa Payoh.

sections.label: TTFS eligibility and race
sections.summary: A Malay/Muslim individual was told by MENDAKI he is not eligible for TTFS because his identity card showed his race is Indian.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, an individual who sees himself as a Malay/Muslim was informed by MENDAKI that he is not eligible for the TTFS scheme because his identity card showed that his race is Indian.

sections.label: Matching grants and self-help groups
sections.summary: A speaker suggests a committee be set up to clarify matters, and says the dollar-for-dollar matching grant to self-help groups and organisations is well received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When this individual was informed that his application to obtain the Certificate of the Malay Community Committee was approved, he thought about the reason given to him for being ineligible for TTFS because his race was Indian.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I suggest that a committee be established for this purpose to make things clear and, at the same time, avoid any confusion in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the dollar-for-dollar matching grant offered by the Government to self-help groups (SHGs) and some voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) as well as Malay/Muslim organisations thus far is well received and has gone a long way in helping these organisations extend their outreach and help to those in need.

sections.label: Government injections to grants
sections.summary: The Government has made injections to various grants, but matching grants have also been reduced or re-allocated from organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over the years, the Government has made injections to the various grants enabling organisations to benefit more from the grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, there have also been instances where the matching grants have been reduced or re-allocated from the organisations.

sections.label: Unclear matching grant eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The eligibility criteria for matching grants are currently unclear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Right now, the eligibility criteria for matching grants are unclear.

sections.label: Asking Ministry to share criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would be willing to share the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that, would the Ministry be willing to share the criteria?

sections.label: Rejection cases and MENDAKI
sections.summary: The speaker says rejection reasons are unclear and asks how many rejection cases MENDAKI has received over the last three to five years and how they are handled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some of the reasons for the rejections are not truly clear and there are speculations and certain conjectures, for example, race could be a reason.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, therefore, how many such cases of rejection have MENDAKI been getting over the last three to five years and how are they handled?

sections.label: Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund
sections.summary: Malay/Muslim organisations were granted the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund in 2014, with an initial $600,000 allocated and increased each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Our Malay/Muslim organisations were granted the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund (MMCDF) in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: An initial amount of $600,000 was allocated and increased each year.

sections.label: AMLA marriage amendments
sections.summary: Last year's AMLA amendments require couples with one party under 21 to attend marriage preparation courses and obtain parental consent before marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, amendments were made to the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) in which there is a provision which requires couples, when one of them is under 21 years old, to attend marriage preparation courses and obtain parental consent before proceeding with their marriage.

sections.label: Singapore Islamic College proposal
sections.summary: The Singapore Islamic College was first proposed in 2016, and the speaker supports it for post-secondary Islamic education needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The proposal for a Singapore Islamic College was first mooted in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: I support the establishment of this college because it can fulfil the need for Islamic education and studies at the post-secondary level for our community.

sections.label: Asatizah Youth Network set up
sections.summary: MUIS set up the Asatizah Youth Network last year to offer youths a safe space for guidance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: In an effort to counter influences that can lead our youths astray, MUIS set up the Asatizah Youth Network (AYN) last year to offer a safe space for youths seeking guidance.

sections.label: MUIS 50th anniversary
sections.summary: The year 2018 marks 50 years since MUIS was established.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The year 2018 marks 50 years since MUIS was established.

sections.label: Committee for Malay/Muslim PMETs
sections.summary: A committee headed by Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Amrin Amin was set up last year to help Malay/Muslim PMETs with training and employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is important that we provide strong support to help the community in this matter so that they can stay relevant in the new economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Hence, I was pleased when a committee headed by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin was set up last year to help Malay/Muslim professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) with training courses and enhancing their employability.

sections.label: Digital payment at coffee shop
sections.summary: Stallholder Maria Arif and her son Nasri Ramli at a Telok Ayer coffee shop offered digital payment via GrabPay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, stallholder Maria Arif and her son Nasri Ramli at a coffee shop in Telok Ayer offered digital payment via GrabPay.

sections.label: Digital awareness and upgrading schemes
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes efforts by agencies and MENDAKI to raise digital awareness, noting upgrading and assistance schemes for low-income workers and PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome efforts by Government agencies and organisations like MENDAKI and MENDAKI Sense to enhance public knowledge and awareness about the digital world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are many upgrading and assistance schemes for the digital economy that are provided not only for low-income workers, but also for PMETs, too.

sections.label: CDC scope and job support
sections.summary: The speaker asks how CDCs will work with the Future Economy Council, citing their 2013 MOU and asking whether residents can be directed to FSCs, CCs, WSG, e2i and career matching providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the scope of what the Community Development Councils (CDCs) have been structured to do has changed significantly over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How do the CDCs plan to work with the Future Economy Council to meet this objective?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2013, the CDCs signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the then-Spring and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) to set up five satellite SME centres in each district.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While providing job support is a very helpful community function, is there a greater scope to draw more operational efficiencies and productivity by directing residents to proceed straight to the Family Service Centres (FSCs) or even the Community Centres (CCs), in collaboration with Workforce Singapore (WSG), the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) centres and the two foreign career matching providers, particularly for residents who need a job urgently?

sections.label: Defeated candidate holding two designations
sections.summary: A first scenario describes a defeated political party candidate holding two designations: branch chairman of a political party and adviser to a PA grassroots organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: First scenario: a member of a political party who contested but was defeated in the general election holds two designations at the same time: one, as the branch chairman of a political party; and two, as an adviser to a PA grassroots organisation.

sections.label: MENDAKI student support numbers
sections.summary: MENDAKI's education programmes support over 20,000 students every year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Today, MENDAKI's education programmes support over 20,000 students every year.

sections.label: MTS student support numbers
sections.summary: For the past five years, MTS has helped over 10,000 students every year across 89 centres island-wide.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the past five years, MTS has been helping over 10,000 students every year, across 89 centres island-wide.

sections.label: Fund disbursement and TTFS revision
sections.summary: Since 2003, $22.9 million from the Fund supported 91,000 students, and the TTFS income eligibility criteria will be revised with three subsidy tiers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since 2003, $22.9 million from the Fund has been disbursed to support 91,000 students, from preschool all the way to the Institute of Technical Education (ITE).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat mentioned, a key Government policy that supports the education of low-income Malay students is the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy scheme (TTFS).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Muhammad Azhari Bin Mohammad Zain is one beneficiary who, despite his challenging financial circumstances, graduated with First Class Honours in Biological Science from Nanyang Technological University (NTU), and he is now a scientist at the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority (AVA).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In this regard, I am pleased to announce that we will revise the TTFS income eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Students from households with a PCI of $1,400 and below will receive 100% subsidy; those with a PCI of between $1,400 and $1,700 will receive $75% subsidy; and those with a PCI of between $1,700 and $2,000 will receive 50% subsidy.

sections.label: Disbursement to 55 partners yearly
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2017, $10 million was disbursed, benefiting around 55 partners per year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2017, $10 million was disbursed, benefiting around 55 partners per year.

sections.label: Decline in minor Muslim marriages
sections.summary: Minor marriages fell from 10% of Muslim marriages in 2007 to 3.6% in 2017, but this group still needs support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: While the proportion of minor marriages has declined from 10% of Muslim marriages in 2007 to 3.6% in 2017, this group still needs support.

sections.label: New minor marriage application requirements
sections.summary: The new requirements will apply to minor marriage applications from 1 October this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The new requirements will apply to minor marriage applications from 1 October this year.

sections.label: MUIS project, madrasah teachers, IB curriculum
sections.summary: MUIS will launch a project later this month with $10 million committed, while financial incentives benefited over 170 madrasah teachers and Madrasah Aljunied Al-Islamiah is on track to offer 27 students an IB curriculum in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS will hold a project launch later this month and has committed $10 million for this project.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, the introduction of the Government-supported financial incentives for madrasah teachers in secular subjects has benefited more than 170 teachers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Second, Madrasah Aljunied Al-Islamiah is on track to offer a small cohort of 27 students an International Baccalaureate (IB) curriculum in 2019.

sections.label: Asatizah Youth Network formation
sections.summary: The Asatizah Youth Network was formed last year with 11 asatizahs to support youths on social media and be a first touchpoint for those in doubt.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Asatizah Youth Network (AYN) was formed last year with 11 asatizahs to offer support and guidance to our youths on social media as well as be the first touchpoint for those in doubt.

sections.label: MUIS five-year AYN plans
sections.summary: Over the next five years, MUIS aims to grow AYN membership, conduct drop-in sessions at Al-Falah Mosque, and train asatizahs in digital media and counselling to counter youth radicalism.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over the next five years, MUIS aims to grow the AYN membership, conduct drop-in sessions for youths at Al-Falah Mosque in Orchard Road, and continue training asatizahs in digital media engagements and counselling techniques to counter youth radicalism.

sections.label: MUIS50 dinner and religious conference
sections.summary: MUIS will hold a MUIS50 Dinner and Awards Ceremony honouring individuals, and an International Religious Conference on religious scholars and institutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS will be holding a special MUIS50 Dinner and Awards Ceremony and presenting awards that honour individuals who have been instrumental to MUIS and Singapore, and also to inspire youths.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS will also hold an International Religious Conference at the end of the year to rally the community on the important role of religious scholars and institutions in shaping a progressive religious life.

sections.label: FFP for ITE students
sections.summary: The FFP benefits about 240 ITE students and complements ITE's education, career guidance and life skills curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Benefiting about 240 ITE students currently, the FFP complements ITE’s education and career guidance and life skills curriculum.

sections.label: PMET proportion increase
sections.summary: The proportion of PMETs rose from one in four in 2007 to one in three in 2017, mostly in education, health, social services and public administration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The proportion of PMETs has increased from one in four in 2007 to one in three in 2017, with a majority in education, health, social services and public administration.

sections.label: PMET Outreach Committee
sections.summary: Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Amrin Amin will lead a PMET Outreach Committee to support Malay/Muslim PMETs' retraining and employability needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We want to help our workers and encourage skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I have asked Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin to lead a PMET Outreach Committee to create a support network for Malay/Muslim PMETs' retraining and employability needs.

sections.label: Digitally-enabled retail neighbourhood
sections.summary: IMDA is working with SMCCI, One Kampong Gelam Association and other partners to create Singapore's first digitally-enabled retail neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) Committee of Supply (COS) speech, IMDA is working together with SMCCI, One Kampong Gelam Association, and other partners to create Singapore's first digitally-enabled retail neighbourhood.

sections.label: TTFS scheme reviewed
sections.summary: The TTFS scheme, provided by the Government and managed by MENDAKI, has been reviewed for children in tertiary education.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For our children in tertiary education, there is good news.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the TTFS scheme, provided by the Government and managed by MENDAKI, has been reviewed.

sections.label: Madrasah Wak Tanjong assistance package
sections.summary: The Government supports Malay/Muslim religious institutions, and MUIS will provide a Comprehensive Assistance Package to Madrasah Wak Tanjong Al Islamiah.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Government is committed to helping the Malay/Muslim community develop institutions that support our religious life, including the institution of madrasahs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that MUIS will be providing a Comprehensive Assistance Package to Madrasah Wak Tanjong Al Islamiah.

sections.label: MUIS $10 million redevelopment project
sections.summary: MUIS has committed $10 million and will launch this redevelopment project later this month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS has committed $10 million and will launch this redevelopment project later this month.

sections.label: First Islamic college in Singapore
sections.summary: The community's desire to build Singapore's first Islamic college is progressing well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The community’s desire to build our first Islamic college in Singapore is progressing well.

sections.label: Digital readiness for Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: The third strategy prepares the Malay/Muslim community to be digitally ready, with plans to make Kampong Glam a digitally enabled retail neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the third strategy is to prepare our Malay/Muslim community to be digitally ready so that we can also seize opportunities in the Digital Economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Today, the majority of Malay/Muslim businesses are still operating in their old ways.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, I am happy with the opportunity to engage members from SMCCI recently to emphasise the importance of embracing digital technology if they do not want their business to be adversely affected in the future.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am also excited with the plans to turn Kampong Glam into the first fully digitally enabled retail neighbourhood.

sections.label: Digitisation of Kampong Glam
sections.summary: Digitising Kampong Glam can help merchants enhance their businesses and uncover its history and heritage for younger generations and the world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: By harnessing technology, the digitisation of Kampong Glam can help merchants enhance their businesses and, at the same time, uncover the rich history and heritage of Kampong Glam, especially to the younger generation, as well as to the whole world.

sections.label: ITE student now MNC analyst
sections.summary: From being a student in ITE, he is now an analyst in a multinational corporation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: From being a student in ITE, he is now an analyst in a multinational corporation (MNC).

sections.label: CDCs SkillsFuture awareness
sections.summary: The CDCs were tasked last year to raise awareness of the SkillsFuture movement for lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Last year, the CDCs were tasked to raise awareness of the SkillsFuture movement to help Singaporeans better understand the importance of lifelong learning.

sections.label: Satellite SME centres at CDCs
sections.summary: The five satellite SME centres at CDCs are part of a larger island-wide network supporting SME growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The five satellite SME centres at CDCs are part of a bigger network of SME centres island-wide that aimed to support the growth of SMEs.

sections.label: Grassroots advisers appointed by Government
sections.summary: Grassroots advisers are appointed by the Government to guide PA grassroots organisations, including explaining unpopular policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Grassroots advisers are appointed by the Government of the day to guide the PA grassroots organisations in carrying out this mission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This includes explaining difficult and sometimes unpopular policies that are necessary for the future of Singapore, such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) hike and foreign manpower policies.

sections.label: Government agencies and political outreach
sections.summary: Government agencies will not conduct activities with any political party for political outreach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: On the collaboration with Government agencies, let me say that Government agencies will not do and conduct any activities with any political party for political outreach.

sections.label: TTFS eligibility criteria revision
sections.summary: About 11,000 students are currently on TTFS, and the question asks how many more will benefit from revised eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: How many more students will benefit from this change of the revision in the eligibility criteria?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, in stock, we have about 11,000 students currently on TTFS.

sections.label: MUIS assistance to MWTI
sections.summary: The question asks what terms and conditions MUIS places on MWTI in accepting financial assistance for its land lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: For Minister Yaacob Ibrahim, I would like to ask regarding the announcement made by the Minister about MUIS rendering financial assistance to help Madrasah Wak Tanjong Al-Islamiyah (MWTI) with the payment of the land lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: So, I just want to know, by accepting this assistance, what are the terms and conditions that are placed upon MWTI by MUIS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: For example, is MWTI required to join the Joint Madrasah System?

sections.label: MWTI resources and teachers
sections.summary: MUIS will provide resources for MWTI's lease, curriculum and teacher professional development so it continues serving students well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The most important thing for us now is to ensure that MWTI continues to perform and serve the students to the best of its ability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, MUIS will pump in resources, as I mentioned in my speech, not just for the lease but also in terms of the curriculum and the professional development of our teachers.

sections.label: Advice for Opposition ward residents
sections.summary: People in Opposition wards wanting something represented to agencies should first approach their MP, the Opposition MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in response to Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap's example, our advice to all our people is this: if the person stays in an Opposition ward, as in the Member's example, if he wants something to be represented to the agencies, the first recourse is to go to his MP, in this case, the Opposition MP.

sections.label: TTFS re-application and budget
sections.summary: Denied TTFS students may re-apply under new conditions and remain eligible, and MOF's Budget will cover more students and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: TTFS is managed in a way such that a student who is once denied, can re-apply based on his or her new conditions and, if eligible for TTFS, will remain so, no matter what changes there are to their circumstances going forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: To the second question, we are still working out the details.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I just want to assure the Member that the Budget would be enough from MOF to allow us to service the increased number of students and also to allow us to run some of the programmes that we are able to do for the benefit of TTFS.

sections.label: Study loan repayments and reserves
sections.summary: Delayed loan repayments have fallen, and a deep dive is ensuring the right loan quantum and repayment ability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We understand sometimes when the circumstances do not allow it, because of circumstances, because they cannot get a job, we are prepared to delay.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: But over the years, the numbers of delayed payments have come down, and I think that is very good news for the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am not at liberty to share the details.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are doing a deep dive to ensure that we have the right policy level to ensure that Malay/Muslim students who need study loans are given the right quantum with an assurance of their ability to pay back because the money does not belong to us, it belongs to the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you check with the National Council of Social Service (NCSS), the guideline is about two to three years of reserves.

sections.label: MENDAKI reserves and financial analysis
sections.summary: Financial analysis covers MENDAKI's overall needs, not just loans, and reserves are being built toward the right balance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: It is not just about the loan, because part of the loan that we are able to save goes into our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, the financial analysis is on not just the loan but the overall needs of MENDAKI in order to service the programmes we have committed to.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am not at liberty to say how much we have now at the moment, but we are trying to build up our reserves so that at the end of the day we can find that right balance.

sections.label: Social mixing among the young
sections.summary: The question asks what the Ministry can do to increase social mixing, especially among the young, amid global instability and terror threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As we contend with political instability and terror threats globally, what can the Ministry do to increase social mixing, especially amongst the young, so that we can continue to grow shared experiences and understanding?

sections.label: IRCC equivalent for class issues
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government has an IRCC-equivalent for discussions on issues of class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: As such, given the utility of the IRCC for the respective discussions on race and religion, does the Government have an IRCC-equivalent for discussion on issues of class?

sections.label: MCCY and SportSG academies clubs
sections.summary: MCCY and SportSG have been rolling out new academies and clubs consistently over the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MCCY and SportSG have been rolling out new academies and clubs consistently over the past two years.

sections.label: Abdul Thaslim running and mentoring
sections.summary: Abdul Thaslim won his school cross-country race three years in a row and now mentors Henderson youths at WeLL Centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Abdul Thaslim did, and the rest is history.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: He won his school’s cross-country race three years in a row and was made one of five running ambassadors for the Standard Chartered Marathon Singapore 2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: All the motivational talks he attended at WeLL Centre and training under SportCares taught him strong values of teamwork, discipline, determination and perseverance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am very proud to share that Abdul Thaslim, now 20, is in the second year of Higher National ITE Certificate (Nitec) in Mechanical Engineering at ITE College West and is currently mentoring our Henderson youths at the WeLL Centre.

sections.label: Vision 2030 sports facility access
sections.summary: Under Vision 2030, MCCY aimed for most Singaporeans to have a sports facility within a 10-minute walk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, under Vision 2030, MCCY announced that the aim was for a majority of Singaporeans to have a sports facility within a 10-minute walk from their home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are currently about 87 pay-to-play school fields, 49 free-to-play fields and 77 indoor sports halls.

sections.label: School sports facilities and Boon Lay hockey village
sections.summary: The passage asks about opening school sports facilities to the public and upgrading the Boon Lay hockey village.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Is it possible to avail the sports facilities in all schools to the public, after school hours, on all weekday evenings?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I wish to ask if MCCY would consider upgrading the current "hockey village" in Boon Lay constituency which is owned and operated by SportSG and in quite an old condition.

sections.label: Singapore Sports Hub cornerstones
sections.summary: The $1.3 billion Singapore Sports Hub was the biggest Public-Private-Partnership project at its inception with three cornerstones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The $1.3 billion new Singapore Sports Hub, mooted as a replacement for this icon, was the biggest Public-Private-Partnership project at its inception, and was noted to have three cornerstones: an integrated hub for sports and entertainment, a commercially viable model, and a national and global icon.

sections.label: NDP Sports Hub cost and viability
sections.summary: The 2016 Sports Hub NDP cost $39.4 million, and the member asks how the Government measures the Hub's viability and connection with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The NDP held in the Sports Hub in 2016 had a bill of $39.4 million, over double the bill for the NDP held at the Floating Platform in the past years, and only costing $1 million less than the SG50 NDP held at the Padang.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even as the Government preaches patience, can the Ministry explain what benchmark it is using to measure the Sports Hub’s viability and success?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the issue of the Hub’s cornerstone as a national icon, there seems to me a real risk that it might become a white elephant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now that the NDP is not going to be held at the Sports Hub most of the time, how will the Government steer or nudge the Sports Hub to have a strong connection with Singaporeans at large?

sections.label: Academies and clubs for sports
sections.summary: MCCY and SportSG have rolled out academies and clubs conducting regular classes in various sports halls and areas to encourage Singaporeans to be active.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To encourage Singaporeans, especially our children and youths, to be physically active and take up sports for leisure, MCCY and SportSG have rolled out several academies and clubs to conduct regular classes for different sports in various sports halls and areas.

sections.label: Team Nila sports volunteers
sections.summary: Team Nila was launched in 2015 to create a common identity for sports volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Team Nila was launched in 2015 to create a common identity for sports volunteers.

sections.label: One Team Singapore fund funding
sections.summary: The One Team Singapore fund launched last October could give elite athletes up to S$100 million, with Government matching donations up to S$50 million from 2017 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The launch of the One Team Singapore fund last October is thus a much-needed shot in the arm for our athletes who want to hone their skills and take their sporting prowess further afield to represent Singapore in prestigious games and competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that under the One Team Singapore initiative, elite athletes could get up to S$100 million in funding, with the Government to match donations of up to S$50 million from Singaporeans and corporate firms from 2017 to 2022.

sections.label: Funding for non-core sports athletes
sections.summary: The member suggests more flexibility in standards so athletes from non-core sports meeting a certain standard are also supported through funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the One Team Singapore initiative helps those involved in core sports, there is a possibility for more flexibility in standards, so that athletes from non-core sports that have achieved a certain standard are also supported through funding that helps them grow their talent and boost our Singapore sporting capabilities and our sporting heritage as well.

sections.label: Tote Board football grant
sections.summary: A January 2017 TODAY online article states SportSG administers an annual grant of some $25 million from the Tote Board for football and the S League.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to an article in TODAY online in January 2017, SportSG administers an annual grant of some $25 million from the Tote Board, a Statutory Board, for the development of football and the S League, our local professional football league.

sections.label: Singapore football ranking and results
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked 173, an all-time low, and the senior national team has not won a competitive match in over a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we are ranked at 173, an all-time low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our senior national team has not won a competitive football match in over a year.

sections.label: S League youth and foreign rules
sections.summary: From this new season, every S League squad must have at least six under-23 players, three under-23 players in the team of 11, and the foreign signings quota is cut from three to two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From this new season, every S League squad will have at least six players who are under the age of 23.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And when the team takes to the field, a minimum of three players in the team of 11 have to be under 23 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And another new rule is that the foreign signings quota will be reduced from three to two.

sections.label: Worst-ever ranking and Tonga
sections.summary: The speaker asks if Singapore is satisfied being has-beens, notes the worst-ever ranking of 173, and hopes Singapore is not racing to be worst-ranked, currently Tonga at 206.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Are we satisfied with continuing to be has-beens in local and regional tournaments in the foreseeable future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are already at our worst-ever ranking at 173, I do hope we are not in the race to be the worst-ranked nation in the world of football, the dubious honour currently belonging to Tonga at 206.

sections.label: National Stadium home of Lions
sections.summary: The FAS and Sports Hub tie-up makes the National Stadium the Lions' home, and the speaker asks whether empty terraces would do justice to the stadium, noting the Maldives match on 23 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, another positive move is the recent tie-up between the FAS and the Sports Hub which makes the National Stadium the home of the Lions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My concern is that with the dismal results and quality of football, will we be doing justice to the magnificent stadium by playing matches with empty terraces?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, it is the performance on the pitch, not rhetoric, aesthetics or partnerships, that will determine how many fans show up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the first competitive match for the Lions this year will be against the Maldives on 23 March at the National Stadium.

sections.label: FIFA ranking drop and masterplan
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether FAS has a masterplan, noting the team dropped 11 notches to 173 in October 2017 while the Philippines, Vietnam and Myanmar improved to 116, 121 and 155.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I would also like to ask whether FAS has come up with a masterplan to heal Singapore football.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: It was reported in the media in October 2017 that our National Football Team has slumped to its lowest ever position in the International Federation of Football Association's (FIFA's) overall ranking, dropping 11 notches from the September 2017 ranking of 162 to 173.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: In contrast, our Asian counterparts, such as the Philippines, Vietnam and Myanmar, have been showing vast improvements in recent years, and their current FIFA rankings are 116, 121 and 155 respectively.

sections.label: WeCare Arts Fund beneficiaries
sections.summary: The WeCare Arts Fund was renewed last year to increase access for the less advantaged, and since 2014 its arts projects involved over 8,000 beneficiaries; the speaker asks if there is an assessment of value and impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Last year, the WeCare Arts Fund was renewed to increase access to the less advantaged groups in our community, the underserved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Since the Fund was started in 2014, the arts projects involved over 8,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Is there any assessment on the value and impact of the programmes on the beneficiaries involved?

sections.label: Singaporeans' arts and culture interest
sections.summary: 2016 Ministry statistics indicate more Singaporeans actively enjoy museums, performing arts and visual arts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The 2016 statistics from the Ministry indicate that more Singaporeans are taking an active interest in arts and culture, enjoying museums, performing arts and visual arts activities.

sections.label: WSQ Work Mentorship Programme
sections.summary: The WSQ Work Mentorship Programme gives junior creative freelancers training and mentorship, and a free legal rights handbook was launched.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The Work Mentorship Programme by Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) aims to give junior creative freelancers a headstart through hands-on-training and mentorship with companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Last year, a free handbook was also launched to educate and inform creative freelancers about their legal rights.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Thus far, how effective has it been in mitigating the problems that freelancers face from errant clients?

sections.label: Government support for arts freelancers
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Government is doing to increase support for freelancers in the arts industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: What is the Government doing to increase support for freelancers within the arts industry?

sections.label: ACSR focus areas
sections.summary: ACSR focuses on defining Singaporean identity in a globalised world and promoting social cohesion among all population segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the moment, ACSR focuses on two key aspects: one, defining the Singaporean identity in a globalised world; two, promoting social cohesion amongst all segments of the population.

sections.label: Singapore's historical regional settlement
sections.summary: Singapore was part of the Srivijaya and Majapahit empires, and excavations confirm it was a thriving 14th century settlement and port.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Historically, Singapore has a deep and rich relationship within the Southeast Asian region; it was part of the Srivijaya and Majapahit empires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Archaeological excavations in Singapore have confirmed that we were more than an insignificant mudflat or sleepy fishing village, as often painted by official narratives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, we were a thriving settlement and port way back from the 14th century.

sections.label: ACSR arts education focus
sections.summary: The ACSR report focuses on Arts Education in school and at community level to bring arts closer to people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ACSR report has a significant focus on Arts Education in school, as well as at a community level, with the aim to bring the arts closer to the people, and also to increase their knowledge of art.

sections.label: Creative intervention solving problems
sections.summary: Creative intervention applies creative thinking to solving problems, communal issues and social issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Creative intervention is about putting creative thinking into solving problems, communal issues and social issues.

sections.label: Social cohesion through engagement
sections.summary: Social cohesion comes from engagement and dialogue, not from watching ad hoc art events, and requires social care first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Social cohesion cannot come from watching ad hoc art events in communities and schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It comes from engagement and dialogue, speaking and listening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to socially care before we can socially cohere.

sections.label: Limited funding for artists
sections.summary: Funding is limited, especially for smaller companies, individual artists and groups, and artists who push boundaries and take risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Funding is limited, especially for smaller companies, individual artists and groups and artists that push boundaries, take risks and create experiment artwork.

sections.label: State as venture capitalist
sections.summary: Once achieved, the state can divert more funding and support innovative, experimental artists like a venture capitalist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Once this is achieved, the state can then divert more funding and play a role similar to that of a venture capitalist, providing support to these artists who are innovative and experimental, and who need a leg up.

sections.label: IPS social capital study
sections.summary: An IPS study found diversity in social networks strengthens social capital, trust, national identity and pride, and OBS camps have involved 6,000 students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, a recent study, conducted by IPS on Social Capital in Singapore found that diversity in social networks among Singaporeans strengthens social capital, trust, national identity and national pride.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Last year, MCCY announced that mixed-cohort camps would be established to bring students from different backgrounds together through the Outward Bound School (OBS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Since its launch, some 6,000 Secondary 3 students from 28 secondary schools have taken part in OBS camps.

sections.label: ASEAN Workplan on Youth
sections.summary: The ASEAN Workplan on Youth 2016 to 2020 is a good start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Workplan on Youth 2016 to 2020 is a good start.

sections.label: Youth economic optimism ranking
sections.summary: A 2015 Citi Foundation and EIU report ranked Singaporean youths aged 13 to 25 32nd out of 35 cities for optimism about their economic future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A report by Citi Foundation and the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) published in 2015 ranked Singaporean youths aged between 13 and 25, 32nd out of 35 cities in terms of optimism about their economic future.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund establishment
sections.summary: Our Singapore Fund was established in August 2016 following from Our Singapore Conversation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Our Singapore Fund was established in August 2016 following from Our Singapore Conversation.

sections.label: Funded projects and eligibility review
sections.summary: It asks how many projects have been funded to date and whether eligibility criteria have been reviewed to encourage more applicants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: How many projects have been funded to date, and has there been any review of the eligibility criteria to encourage more people to apply for the fund?

sections.label: Helping smaller volunteer-run charities
sections.summary: It asks how the Government can help smaller volunteer-run charities understand running a charitable organisation and meet transparency and accountability standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: How can the Government help these smaller volunteer-run charities to better understand the complexities of running a charitable organisation and help them meet the standards of transparency and accountability?

sections.label: Discerning real from fake donation drives
sections.summary: It asks how the Government can help citizens discern real donation drives from fake ones and know what to look out for, especially online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: In light of these challenges, how can the Government help citizens to discern between a real donation drive from a fake one, and help them to understand what to look out for when donating to charities, especially in the case of online charity donation drives?

sections.label: MCCY five years achievements
sections.summary: It states that since MCCY's formation five years ago it built the three Cs and developed cultural, community, sports and youth landscapes, listing SG50 highlights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since the formation of MCCY five years ago, we have been working tirelessly to build the three "Cs" that are the cornerstones of a strong society – a Caring people, a Cohesive Society and a Confident nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have developed a vibrant cultural, community, sports and youth landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We introduced free entry to museums and cultural institutions and kickstarted ActiveSG for Singaporeans from all walks of life to have greater access to the arts, heritage and sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The year 2015 was our Golden Jubilee, and SG50 saw many highlights, such as the inscription of the much-loved Singapore Botanic Gardens as our first United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage Site, the opening of the National Gallery and hosting of the 28th SEA Games and 8th ASEAN Para Games.

sections.label: Arts, sports, volunteerism, donations rates
sections.summary: It states 2015 arts attendance, 2016 sports participation, volunteerism rise from 2014 to 2016, and donation increase from 2013 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Seventy-eight percent attended at least one arts and culture activity in 2015, and 61% participated in sports regularly in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Our volunteerism rate doubled from 18% in 2014 to 35% in 2016, and donations increased by over $200 million, from $2.5 billion in 2013 to $2.7 billion in 2015.

sections.label: Our SG Heritage Plan funding
sections.summary: It states the first five-year instalment of Our SG Heritage Plan will start this year, with $66 million set aside.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Kok Heng Leun that our history is an important part of what makes us Singaporean and is expressed through our arts, culture and heritage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This year, we will kickstart the first five-year instalment of Our SG Heritage Plan, our first long-term comprehensive national masterplan to safeguard and promote our shared heritage for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Sixty-six million dollars have been set aside to implement this plan.

sections.label: UNESCO intangible cultural heritage convention ratified
sections.summary: It announces Singapore ratified the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage on 22 February 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Everyone in the community can play a part in keeping our shared heritage alive and vibrant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we have ratified the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage on 22 February 2018.

sections.label: Legislation changes for heritage preservation
sections.summary: It states relevant legislation will be changed within two years to support heritage preservation and safeguard archaeological history.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In addition, we will also be making changes to the relevant legislation within the next two years to better support the preservation of both our tangible and intangible heritage, and to safeguard our archaeological history more effectively.

sections.label: BRIDGE dialogue on race and religion
sections.summary: It states BRIDGE was introduced in March last year to support community-led dialogue on sensitive race and religion issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In a global climate of growing intolerance, it is important that we bridge this knowledge gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And that is why we introduced BRIDGE in March last year, to facilitate and support community-led initiatives that use dialogue to deepen understanding on sensitive issues of race and religion.

sections.label: Ask Me Anything Islam series
sections.summary: It states the Ask Me Anything (Islam) series run by the Association of Muslim Professionals kicked off with success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Ask Me Anything (Islam) series run by the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP) kicked off with success.

sections.label: SGSecure Community Network religious organisations
sections.summary: The SGSecure Community Network was established to reach out to and build crisis management capabilities in all religious organisations, beyond the 1,500 IRCC members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In line with our national SGSecure movement against terrorism, we established the SGSecure Community Network (SGCN) last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The network will reach out to, connect with, and build crisis management capabilities in all religious organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This network will go beyond the 1,500 member-strong IRCCs to include those that are not members.

sections.label: Youth Conversations kickstart April
sections.summary: The Ministry will kickstart the Youth Conversations in April this year to bring together youths willing to work with one another or Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Many are willing and able to step up, take action and work with one another or with Government on ideas and projects that will take us forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, my Ministry will kickstart the Youth Conversations in April this year to bring them together.

sections.label: Digital platform for youth conversations
sections.summary: A digital platform will be developed to facilitate real-time conversations across large online communities and enable participants to build and sustain connections.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will use technology to stay relevant and connected with our youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will be developing a digital platform that can facilitate real-time conversations across large online communities and enable participants to build and sustain connections with one another.

sections.label: ActiveSG sporting opportunities expansion
sections.summary: ActiveSG launched in 2014 expanded everyday sporting opportunities for Singaporeans, with close to 1.4 million members now on board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: With the launch of ActiveSG in 2014, we saw an expansion of everyday sporting opportunities for all Singaporeans to participate and bond through sport.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We now have close to 1.4 million ActiveSG members on board.

sections.label: ActiveSG Academies and Clubs launched
sections.summary: Since 2016, 10 ActiveSG Academies and Clubs have been launched, reaching out to about 25,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since 2016, we have launched 10 ActiveSG Academies and Clubs, reaching out to about 25,000 participants.

sections.label: More ActiveSG Academies and Clubs
sections.summary: More Academies and Clubs will be rolled out in sports such as aquatics, canoeing, dance fit, gymnastics, martial arts, table tennis, volleyball and youth sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: At a recent ActiveSG Football Academy end-of-season festival, besides the children, the AFA Dads had their own tournament, too!

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that we will roll out more Academies and Clubs in sports, such as aquatics, canoeing, dance fit, gymnastics, martial arts, table tennis, volleyball and youth sports.

sections.label: Sports-in-Precinct and Dual-Use facilities
sections.summary: Six more Sports-in-Precinct facilities will be developed, and the remaining 300 or so Dual-Use Scheme facilities will progressively open by around 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Following the pilot projects in Boon Lay and Jurong Spring, we will be developing six more Sports-in-Precinct facilities in Bukit Batok, Keat Hong, Hong Kah North, Nee Soon Central, Taman Jurong and Tampines North constituencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Under the Dual-Use Scheme, we now have close to 260 facilities, including Indoor Sports Halls, courts and fields opened for shared use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will progressively open up the remaining 300 or so Dual-Use Scheme facilities by around 2020.

sections.label: War on Diabetes and Active Health
sections.summary: MOH declared War on Diabetes last year, and the Ministry will play its part through Active Health, a national social movement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To meet the challenges of an ageing society, the Ministry of Health (MOH) declared War on Diabetes last year as a national effort to keep our population healthy as we age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I agree with Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Darryl David that sports and exercise are also important for health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Therefore, in this war, my Ministry will play our part through Active Health, a national social movement to spur Singaporeans to take ownership of their health and wellness, help one another meet their goals and to celebrate living better through sports together.

sections.label: Joseph's Active Health results
sections.summary: After starting his Active Health journey and three follow-up sessions, Joseph lost about six kg and saw improvements in blood pressure and BMI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since starting his Active Health journey and after three follow-up sessions, Joseph lost about six kg and has seen improvements in his blood pressure and body mass index (BMI).

sections.label: Four more Active Health Labs
sections.summary: Four more Active Health Labs are planned at Bishan, Jurong East, Sengkang and Woodlands sports centres in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In addition to the Active Health Labs at Our Tampines Hub and Heartbeat@Bedok, we plan to roll out four more at Bishan, Jurong East, Sengkang and Woodlands sports centres in the coming year, so that there is a lab accessible to every Singaporean.

sections.label: Volunteering interest versus actual volunteering
sections.summary: Just slightly over half of those interested in volunteering their time have actually volunteered in any activity in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Just slightly over half of those interested in volunteering their time have actually volunteered in any activity in the past year.

sections.label: SG Cares platform
sections.summary: SG Cares provides a platform that will encourage and support individuals, corporates and organisations to work together for the common good.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: SG Cares provides a platform that will encourage and support individuals, corporates and organisations to work together for the common good.

sections.label: MCCY role and SG Cares
sections.summary: MCCY's key responsibility is creating platforms for Singaporeans of different backgrounds to interact, building a cohesive, inclusive and caring society, with SG Cares mobilising resources for communities in need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Amid the global landscape of increased anti-globalisation sentiments and disruptive technologies, Singapore is facing economic and industry shifts, the need for skills upgrading, and challenges from an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: These rapid developments present opportunities but also give rise to societal issues, such as unequal income growth, as well as racial and religious extremism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The key responsibility of MCCY is thus to create more platforms for Singaporeans of different backgrounds to interact, facilitating a deeper understanding for one another, in turn, building a cohesive, inclusive and caring society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Through the SG Cares movement, the Government will work with corporates and citizens to mobilise resources and match them with the communities in need.

sections.label: Healthcare staff arts training
sections.summary: Almost 400 healthcare staff from 89 community care facilities have been equipped to run arts programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Almost 400 healthcare staff from 89 community care facilities have been equipped with the capability to run arts programmes.

sections.label: Silver Arts touring and WeCare Fund
sections.summary: Silver Arts commissioned programmes will tour community care and social service facilities, and the WeCare Arts Fund with CDCs is renewed with $1 million over two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To broaden outreach to underserved and less mobile seniors, we will also tour Silver Arts commissioned programmes, featuring Singapore short films, to facilities in the community care and social service sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We announced last year that the WeCare Arts Fund, in partnership with CDCs, would be renewed with $1 million over the next two years.

sections.label: Fund support since 2014
sections.summary: Since its initiation in 2014, the fund has supported 170 centres, close to 350 programmes and over 8,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since its initiation in 2014, the fund has supported 170 centres, close to 350 programmes and over 8,000 beneficiaries.

sections.label: Programmes since March 2016
sections.summary: Since March 2016, over 200 such programmes have served about 8,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since March 2016, over 200 such programmes have served about 8,000 participants.

sections.label: YCS growth and overseas service
sections.summary: Since 2014 YCS expanded from 90 to over 14,000 volunteers, providing over 3,000 local opportunities annually, and over 4,000 youths joined overseas service-learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2014, YCS has expanded from 90 volunteers to more than 14,000 and works with partners to provide over 3,000 local volunteering opportunities annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Last year, more than 4,000 youths from ITEs, polytechnics, universities and working adults embarked on such overseas service-learning opportunities through social service organisations in our region, where they organised projects that benefited local and overseas communities.

sections.label: Team dedication and Immersion Programme
sections.summary: The team showed dedication and resilience, and the Immersion Programme will have its first run in April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The team demonstrated strong dedication in meeting the community's needs and resilience in overcoming setbacks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We also have the Immersion Programme, which will have its first run in April.

sections.label: Team Nila volunteer numbers
sections.summary: As of February there are about 17,700 Team Nila volunteers, with a target of 18,000 by month's end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As of February, there are about 17,700 Team Nila volunteers with a target to reach 18,000 by the end of this month.

sections.label: CPR and AED trained volunteers
sections.summary: In emergencies or crises, 750 volunteers trained in CPR and AED use could provide community support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In times of emergency or crises, we have 750 volunteers trained in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and the use of automated external defibrillators (AED) who could provide community support.

sections.label: SportCares youths volunteering hours
sections.summary: Beneficiaries are encouraged to give back, with 400 SportCares youths contributing 7,000 volunteering hours last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Beneficiaries are encouraged to give back to the community, with 400 SportCares youths contributing 7,000 volunteering hours last year.

sections.label: Disability Sports Master Plan progress
sections.summary: Since 2016 two Centres of Expertise, three inclusive gyms and four disability sports programmes were launched, with more planned in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since 2016, we have launched two Centres of Expertise and three inclusive gyms, as well as four disability sports programmes under the Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Over 2,000 Persons with Disabilities have visited our gyms and more than 300 have participated in the programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: SportSG, through ActiveSG, will also be launching two more inclusive gyms and more disability sports programmes, such as Wheelchair Tennis, in 2018.

sections.label: Fund status and supported projects
sections.summary: Since its August 2016 launch, the Fund has supported over 100 projects reaching over 200,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To address Ms Rahayu Mahzam’s question on the Fund’s status, since its launch in August 2016, over 100 projects across the arts, heritage, community and volunteerism sectors have been supported, reaching out to over 200,000 residents, whether as participants, partners or volunteers.

sections.label: Charity shared services guidance
sections.summary: From mid-2018, umbrella bodies will help set up shared services and legislative guidance for charities' regulatory compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Starting in mid-2018, we will work with the umbrella bodies to set up shared services and develop legislative guidance to help charities comply with the regulatory requirements.

sections.label: ACSR review and arts plans
sections.summary: Efforts have borne fruit; progress under the ACSR will be reviewed at its midway point, and plans for literary, performing and visual arts are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We believe our efforts have borne fruit and thank Mr Kok Heng Leun for his suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will review and share how far we have come under the ACSR and the areas for improvement at its midway point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Mr Kok Heng Leun and Dr Lim Wee Kiak also asked about our strategies and plans to further develop the arts sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We are reviewing our plans in the literary, performing and visual arts this year to outline the strategies for each art form as we head towards 2025.

sections.label: Further details by year end
sections.summary: Further details will be shared by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Further details will be shared by the end of this year.

sections.label: SingLit books for schools
sections.summary: All primary and secondary schools will be given a set of SingLit books.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   We will be giving all primary and secondary schools a set of SingLit books.

sections.label: New local music platform
sections.summary: NAC will launch a new platform next month, Hear65, to promote local music.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NAC will be launching a new platform next month to promote local music, Hear65.

sections.label: Support framework for arts freelancers
sections.summary: MOM and NAC consulted freelancers and employers, developed a Support Framework, and will set up a national resource centre for arts freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In 2017, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and NAC consulted freelancers and key employers to gather their feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We have developed a Support Framework that fosters fair and progressive employment conditions and meets our freelancers’ professional development needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NAC and the National Heritage Board (NHB) will be early adopters of MOM’s Tripartite Standard for Contracting Self-Employed Persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Independent artists raised a wish list for better access to resources, training and networking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will, therefore, set up a national resource centre, in both physical and digital forms, dedicated to supporting the needs of arts freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The centre will conduct training programmes, as well as provide resources and services on individual rights and responsibilities, career development and finance.

sections.label: Museum-based learning in primary art
sections.summary: The revised primary art syllabus recommends museum-based learning as a core learning experience starting this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Starting this year, museum-based learning is recommended as a core learning experience in the revised primary art syllabus.

sections.label: MCCY ASEAN youth initiatives
sections.summary: MCCY will renew the Singapore-ASEAN Youth Fund and host an ASEAN eSports tournament this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For our chairmanship, MCCY will launch three initiatives to empower, engage and nurture the many diverse groups of youths in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: First, we will renew the Singapore-ASEAN Youth Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Since the establishment of the Fund in 2007, we have supported many meaningful and sustainable projects which have benefited over 22,000 ASEAN youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Second, we will host an ASEAN eSports tournament this year, encompassing a regional League of Legends tournament.

sections.label: ASEAN Youth Fellowship programme
sections.summary: MCCY will introduce the ASEAN Youth Fellowship, an annual platform for young leaders across 3P sectors in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Third, we will introduce the ASEAN Youth Fellowship programme, an annual platform for young leaders across 3P sectors in ASEAN to interact with and better understand one another, creating a closer-knit ASEAN community.

sections.label: Customised support for Team Singapore athletes
sections.summary: Customised support for selected Team Singapore athletes will begin with $2 million for the Asian Games and Asian Para Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Following a review of past competitions, we will be introducing customised support for selected Team Singapore athletes in the lead up to major games over a rolling two-year period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: It will begin with $2 million set aside this year to cover the upcoming Asian Games and Asian Para Games.

sections.label: OTSF donations and government matching
sections.summary: Over $1.5 million has been raised for OTSF, with the Government providing one-for-one matching of up to $50 million over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In just a few months, over $1.5 million has been raised for OTSF so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Government is providing one-for-one matching of up to $50 million for these donations over five years.

sections.label: FAS S League revamp
sections.summary: FAS has announced a revamp of the S League to address youth development, capability development, cost efficiency, and football culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: To raise the standard of play amongst our National Teams, the Football Association of Singapore (FAS) has announced a revamp of the S League to address four key areas – youth development, capability development, cost efficiency, and building a vibrant football culture.

sections.label: Encouraging donations to worthy causes
sections.summary: MCCY promotes many worthy causes and will work with MOF to encourage people to consider making donations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: There is a very broad range of worthy causes, many of which MCCY has been promoting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We will work together with MOF to encourage people to think about making those donations.

sections.label: Mediation requests and freelancer contracts
sections.summary: NAC has received few mediation requests, and NAC and NHB likely cannot require vendors to adopt the model for freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Regarding the need for mediation when disputes arise, so far, the NAC has not received many of such requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As to whether NAC or NHB will also require its vendors or contractors to adopt the same model when they deal with freelancers, as our institutions do not have a direct contract with these freelancers as mentioned, we probably will not be able to do so.

sections.label: Arts charity, centre and public art
sections.summary: Minister supports appealing to the President on arts charity, notes a centre opening this year, and is listing sites for public art.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I will respond to Mr Kok Heng Leun's suggestion about appealing to the President to elevate the prominence of arts in charity efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I think this is an excellent suggestion and we will be very happy to work with the arts community to put forth the proposal for the President's Office's consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: This centre is scheduled to open this year and we look forward to it bringing rich performing traditions closer to the community and we look forward also to the arts groups based there to be better connected and engaged with the local community and the larger community as it promotes a greater appreciation of traditional arts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: On the question of maintenance of public art works, what we are doing now is to come up with a list and approaching different landowners to offer their sites for public art works to be created and displayed.

sections.label: FIFA ranking and FAS funding
sections.summary: The Minister hopes the FIFA ranking will rise over time and will work with and scrutinise FAS on its KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Of course, hopefully, our ranking in FIFA will rise, but that is something that we know will take time, But we will work closely with and also scrutinise FAS closely, based on its funding received, to make sure that the KPIs are met.

sections.label: NAC help for freelancer disputes
sections.summary: The question asks whether NAC would step in to help freelancers deal with disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Would NAC be willing to step in to help these freelancers in dealing with all these disputes?

sections.label: Grant contracts and longer periods
sections.summary: Each grant approval has a contract between NAC and the artist, and a longer period beyond one year can be negotiated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For each grant approval, there will be a contract between NAC and the artist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I am sure, with valid reasons, requesting a longer period beyond one year, that could be negotiated and agreed upon.
